title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers
implementation_kind: independent compact adaptation; no upstream file vendored

retained: overlapping univariate patch tokens with repeat-last end padding
one linear patch projection shared across all channels
one position embedding and Transformer stack shared across all channels
shared channel-wise attention and feed-forward paths implemented by folding channels into the batch; train BatchNorm statistics pool across B*C and patch positions
vanilla multi-head attention, feed-forward residual blocks and temporal BatchNorm
residual attention scores across encoder layers
both attention output projection dropout and attention residual dropout before Add+Norm
learnable pe=zeros position embedding initialized uniformly in [-0.02,0.02] and shared across channels
adapted: forecasting horizon head replaced by a single ordered linear D-dimensional window-average-velocity task adapter
task adapter flattens C,D_model,N_patch in this order and learns separate coefficients for fixed gyro/accelerometer and x/y/z channel identities; optional input dropout precedes its linear map
RevIN omitted because denormalizing six sensor channels into a 2D/3D velocity target is not dimensionally defined
gravity-world six-axis IMU input and 2D/3D average-velocity targets are benchmark adaptations

task_adapter.causality: window_noncausal; attention uses the full observed window
task_adapter.upstream_forecast_channel_identity: preserved even with a shared forecasting head
